newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals settle modestly weaker.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals settle modestly weaker.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based precious metal futures settled slightly weaker on Monday, reflecting marginal weakness in gold bullion prices and a slight firming of the yen against the dollar, traders said.

TOCOM most-active August 1997 gold futures edged to a fresh life-of-contract high of 1,353 yen per gram early in the session, buoyed by trade house buying, but later retraced as the yen firmed and the bullion market came under light selling pressure, traders said.
The contract ended one yen lower at 1,347 yen per gram, while the remaining months were one yen higher to four lower.
Gold bullion ended at $379.70/$380.00 an ounce, off slightly from New York's closing at $380.20/70 and below the closely watched $380 level.
One trader said the spot market now appeared set to retest $378 as it attempted to build a base following last week's dip to an 18-month-low of $376.90.
Traders said the market drew no inspiration from Friday's surprising U.S. jobs data, which fell by 40,000 compared with analysts' average forecast of a gain of 166,000.
Yen-based futures in the other precious metals also ended flat to weaker after erasing modest gains early in the day.
Most-active August platinum ended unchanged at 1,369 yen per gram. It traded from 1,372, a 3-1/2-week high, to 1,367.
One Japanese trader said that, despite near-term weakness, uncertainty about Russian platinum stocks could buoy the market in the medium term.
August palladium settled two yen lower at 430 yen per gram while August silver was off 1.2 yen at 177.5 yen per 10 grams.
